items.title: Dolly Douroux Adams Interview, 1962-04-18
items.q: Then this one here, that's my oldest boy. He was just fresh in from the Army. And Gerald was then 16 and Placif was 14. That's the two boys you've seen at the preservation hall. Well, we started out a trio there.

ctx.x: So you've always been in family bands most of the time. That's right. Still have you.

And I played for years with them until Oivin died. And Lawrence became very ill. Then I had to look for another way. Then this one here, that's my oldest boy. He was just fresh in from the Army. And Gerald was then 16 and Placif was 14. That's the two boys you've seen at the preservation hall. Well, we started out a trio there. And we've been together. Well, I said a trio. We first started the trio because Placif was in the Army. And when he came back, it was four pieces. And then we went along there.

Well, I think of it. I wonder if there's anything else you could tell us about your father. Since, as I say, we never did get much information about the different bands. You say he played the Eureka. Did he play mostly brass bands or did he play in dance orchestras too?
